decisions_made: Per the delegation's continuation note, started with Duality.lean (420 lines, smallest of the 8 count-3-tier files at cycle 20's close), then worked down smaller-first: RestrictedMCS.lean (437), Completeness.lean (483), Chronicle/ChronicleTypes.lean (522), Temporal/Metalogic/MCS.lean (538).

For Duality.lean's 4 linter.flexible sites (bare simp [X] then rw [...] pattern), used declaration-scoped set_option linter.flexible false in on the 2 enclosing theorems rather than manual simp-only reconstruction, per the cycle-20 finding that a bare simp [X]'s full-default-set closure isn't visible without interactive simp? output.

For RestrictedMCS.lean's 2 linter.flexible sites (a single well-understood lemma unfold, simp [Set.mem_insert_iff] at h), attempted manual reconstruction as simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff] at h per the cycle-19 guidance favoring manual fixes for simple, well-understood patterns, and verified by rebuild before committing.

For Temporal ChronicleTypes.lean's 13 dupNamespace warnings on the Chronicle structure and c0-c5' condition defs, did NOT attempt a rename to clear the warning (would alter the public API used by downstream files, out of hygiene-only scope) -- instead narrowed to 10 per-declaration set_option linter.dupNamespace false in lines, matching the identical, already-accepted pattern in the Bimodal counterpart file (BXCanonical/Chronicle/ChronicleTypes.lean, still in the worklist) confirmed via that file's own file-level suppression and module docstring cross-reference.

For Temporal ChronicleTypes.lean's 24 longLine warnings, fixed all of them by wrapping have-statement type annotations onto continuation lines (pure whitespace change, no term-content altered), rather than narrowing via suppression, since this category is always mechanically fixable.

For Temporal MCS.lean's 3 identical unusedSimpArgs sites, collected all 8 flagged-unused-argument warnings per site before editing (per the cycle-19 rule), then used a single replace_all Edit across all 3 identical occurrences rather than 3 separate edits, verified by one rebuild.

Ran the full 8-step CSLib CI pipeline (build --wfail --iofail, checkInitImports, lint-style, mk_all, lake shake, lake lint, lake test, sorry/axiom/vacuous grep census) once at cycle close rather than after each individual file, in addition to the mandatory per-file scoped rebuild + downstream-importer rebuild before each commit, matching this dispatch's explicit hard constraint of committing only when each file is green.

Stopped after 5 files (rather than continuing into Saturation.lean/Soundness.lean or attempting the count-6 Interface.lean) to leave adequate budget for the full CI re-verification pass and an accurate plan/handoff update, consistent with prior cycles' practice of not force-finishing Phase 5 in one cycle.

New findings this cycle: (1) when a structure/namespace name intentionally collides with its enclosing namespace (the Chronicle pattern, confirmed identical in both the Temporal and Bimodal BXCanonical trees per each file's own module docstring), the resulting dupNamespace warnings are a correct, permanent narrowing target, not a fixable warning -- renaming would alter the definition and is out of hygiene-only scope, so apply set_option linter.dupNamespace false in per declaration (structure + each condition def) rather than attempting a rename; (2) longLine warnings on have h : DerivationTree ... := ... are always mechanically fixable by wrapping the type annotation onto its own indented continuation line with zero term-content change -- rebuild after wrapping to confirm no elaboration change; (3) when a simp only [...] blanket-replacement candidate for unusedSimpArgs recurs verbatim at multiple call sites in one file, a single replace_all Edit handles every site in one pass -- but only after confirming (via the collected warning list, not assumption) that every site has the exact same fully-reduced argument list. Cycle-20 findings remain relevant: (a) a bare simp [X] (not simp only [X]) pulling in the full default simp set is a strong signal to prefer declaration-scoped set_option linter.flexible false in over manual reconstruction, since the full set's closure isn't visible without interactive simp? output -- reserve manual simp only reconstruction for simple, single-lemma, well-understood cases (reconfirmed this cycle on RestrictedMCS.lean); (b) when scripting multi-site set_option ... in insertion, insert above the preceding doc comment block, not between it and the declaration -- the cycle-6 parse hazard recurs with scripted insertion specifically; (c) a file's style.openClassical suppression targeting a persistent, non-in open Classical correctly bottoms out at 1 remaining blanket line, not 0 -- this is the correct end state, not incomplete work; (d) lake lint's unusedArguments findings remain out of scope, do not fix opportunistically; (e) when several unusedSimpArgs warnings flag different unused arguments on the same simp only [...] line, collect every warning for that line before editing, apply the fully-reduced argument list in one edit; (f) when re-deriving the worst-offender list, filter to fs > 0 before the upstream gate.
